The Trump administration fired about 400 Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) employees beginning February 14, 2025, as part of sweeping federal workforce cuts led by Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), raising concerns about aviation safety. 
Among those fired were 26 aviation safety assistants, each typically supporting 10 inspectors, as well as maintenance mechanics at 18 air traffic control facilities. 
Union representatives warned that the cuts would increase workloads for remaining staff, potentially affecting radar maintenance, flight navigation updates and safety inspections.
Source: AP

However, the ‘cold war’-style dynamics of armed truces combined with localized fighting goes back thousands of years to the ancient Persian-Roman rivalry spanning from the late first century BC through the seventh century AD.
Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei revived the concept and the related idea of “no war, [no negotiation” during Trump’s 2018-2020 ‘maximum pressure’ campaign](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/69009), which saw the US withdraw from the nuclear deal, reintroduction of tough sanctions, tit-for-tat tanker seizures, proxy attacks, terror designations, the downing of an American spy drone over Hormuz, the US assassination of one of the IRGC’s top commanders, and retaliatory Iranian missile strikes on US bases in Iraq.

🇦🇺 Australia and the Philippines upgrade defense ties with a focus on China
Australia and the Philippines signed a new Defense Cooperation Arrangement on Sunday, upgrading a 1995 pact, Bloomberg reports.
The deal, signed in Manila with Australian PM Anthony Albanese in attendance, covers maritime awareness and information sharing, joint exercises, disaster response, training and defense infrastructure. Albanese also announced new Australian investment in maritime domain awareness, including drone technology and training. 
Australia has been taking part in building defense infrastructure at a series of bases across the Philippines in recent years, making claims about China’s “aggressive tactics” in the South China Sea. 
China, for its part, has repeatedly rejected such allegations, noting that Australia was in “no position to interfere in the maritime issues between countries concerned.”
